subject.title: [Feature]: Script to restore session history archived by new daily-reset mechanism (introduced v2026.2+)

question: Should OpenClaw solve reset archive recovery through read-only family history only, a doctor-owned restore/re-index command, or both?
rationale: Archive recovery changes session identity, retention, and access to sensitive transcript history, so automation should not choose the permanent API or mutation boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Land read-only family history first
options.body: Use the bounded includeFamily-style path as the supported retrieval mechanism before adding any archive-mutating command.

options.title: Add doctor-owned restore/re-index
options.body: Create a deliberate recovery command for already affected users that preserves source metadata and explains retention/security consequences.

options.title: Reject mutation-style restore
options.body: Track only read-only discovery/export surfaces and avoid archive-to-active renames in core.

recommendation.title: Land read-only family history first
recommendation.body: Use the bounded includeFamily-style path as the supported retrieval mechanism before adding any archive-mutating command.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current-main/release routing candidate for the active reset archive fallback and related session-history release surface.
